key_insight: Laya-IsoToken enables clinical coding systems to switch codebooks without target-labeled training notes by separating text evidence extraction from code definitions.
clinical_relevance: The approach could reduce annotation burden when hospitals update diagnostic classifications, reimbursement groupers, or coding languages.
method: Train a clinical span reader once, using a frozen multilingual concept space and no per-code classifier parameters.
Compile public target code descriptions into alignment operators in under three seconds.
Route unfamiliar concepts to offline language-model verification using a geometric residual.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 62.6% Micro-F1 on 32,804 ICD-9 discharges, a 5.4-point ICD-10 F1 gain over semantic crosswalks on unseen patients, and 40.6% ICD-10 Micro-F1 with offline verification on 1,000 summaries.
watch_item: Real-world generalizability and workflow impact require prospective evaluation; zero invalid codes in the reported verifier evaluation does not establish coding accuracy or clinical safety.
paper_title: Laya-IsoToken: Day-One Clinical Codebook Switching via Closed-Form Operator Compilation
